title: Apogee: new hand, astronomer's charts
question: You liked the astronomer's chart, so the whole hand is astronomical artifacts. The roll dealt Glasplåt. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Glasplåt
options.lineage: Astrograph glass plates with the réseau grid and the plate computers' ink annotations
options.thesis: Each Projekt is an exposed plate: Scopes are stars on glass, ringed in ink, and earlier exposures show where they were.
materials: pale glass ground with a fine réseau grid
inked rings: madder → violet → ultramarine with Läge
options.viewport: Dark plate-envelope rail with Funktionsområden; the plate fills the work area with a label strip (plate number, exposed at, by whom); a plate log on the right lists Scopes by Läge with Ägare and a bar for time at the current Läge.
options.risk: The ink ring is small; on a projector the Läge colour reads from the ring and label, not a filled dot.

raised.raise: The plate owns the work area; chrome stays out of its way.
A Scope that moved since you last looked keeps its ring lit until you have seen it.
Time at the current Läge is drawn as an exact-length bar in the log, so a stuck Scope is visible as length.

options.label: Solbana
options.lineage: Sun-path diagrams and the almanac's sunrise–sunset tables
options.thesis: The hill is the sun's arc: uphill is morning, the crest is noon, done is sunset.
materials: sky band whose colour is the Läge scale
each Scope a sun with a drop line to the horizon
options.viewport: Night-blue top bar with Funktionsområden; a sky band behind the hill runs dawn blue → noon gold → evening red, which is the Läge scale itself; a row of Scope cards under the horizon.
options.risk: The most familiar of the hand, and the one most runs would land on; the sky band edges toward decoration if overdone.

options.label: Spektrogram
options.lineage: Glass spectrogram plates on a viewing box
options.thesis: Each Scope is an emission line standing on the hill; Läge is wavelength, from violet to H-alpha red.
options.viewport: Charcoal shell; Scopes rise as coloured lines from the baseline to the hill; state is line form: a stuck Scope is dashed at half height, the latest change doubled.
options.case: Holds audience: it is literally an astronomer's chart and the colour scale is physical. Loses on clarity: lines read less directly than dots and a dark screen suffers on a meeting-room projector.
options.risk: Dark ground in bright meeting rooms and Notion's white pages.

options.label: Pulsar
options.lineage: The CP 1919 pulsar plot, stacked white lines on black
options.thesis: A Funktionsområde is a stack of pulses: every Projekt's hill one white line, each Scope a peak on it.
materials: colour only as code blocks for the open Projekt
options.viewport: Black overview where all Projekt stack as ridgelines; the open Projekt is drawn heavier with its Scopes decoded into colour blocks above the peaks.
options.case: Holds clarity for leaders scanning: one glance shows where every Projekt's work bunches. Loses audience: an album-cover reference, and dark again.
options.risk: Peaks replace dots, so dragging a single Scope needs its own Projekt view.

options.label: Vertical feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole screen.
options.viewport: One Projekt per screen, snap to the next.
options.risk: No astronomy, no tie to the audience.
options.kept: The chart owns the work area.

options.label: Boarding pass and gate board
options.thesis: A changed row stays lit until you notice it.
options.kept: Moved Scopes stay marked until seen.

options.label: Labanotation
options.kept: Time at a Läge drawn as exact length.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS project tool with a grey hill and blue dots.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, hill chart in a card, Scope table below.
canonCard.risk: You already passed on it; indistinguishable from every project tool.
